## Verdict: REJECT (the previous iteration's key-limit fix changed behaviour that one criterion requires to stay unchanged)

This pull request is not ready to merge: iteration two tightened the `_meta` key limit in the one shared metadata helper so that it counts the declared `progressToken` too, and that tightening also reaches a server with no rule-set file, where acceptance criterion thirty-four requires a request that runs today to run with the same result.
Rule applied: rule 1 — a checklist FAIL at or above the threshold → REJECT

## Code Review Findings

### 🔴 Critical

- VC-195: FAIL (critical) — With no rule-set file configured, a `query_database` request that runs today runs with the same result, no request is refused for missing rule-set `_meta`, and the agent's memory-write tools follow `memory.save_queries` and `memory.save_text_memories` as today. [src/sqllens/server.py:243-256] — fix the code, or have the issue author amend this criterion

  <details><summary>Evidence</summary>

  criteria.json read: every element is {criterion,text} and criterion 34 is present, so it counts. Rule-set-gated paths conform: query_database.py selects a rule set only when cfg.rule_sets.loaded is not None (diff 2226-2233), so no request is refused for missing rule-set _meta without a file. factory.py `allow_memory_writes = allow_memory_writes and rule_sets is None` leaves memory-write tools to memory.save_* when unset. The user resolver, guards, redactor and sql_mode removal are all gated on rule_sets being non-None. Trigger split: the code condition in server.py:256 `type(extra) is not dict or len(extra) > 64 or len(sent) > 64` is NOT gated on a rule-set file. The `len(sent) > 64` operand counts model_fields_set (server.py:243), which includes the declared progressToken. A no-rule-set request with progressToken plus exactly 64 undeclared _meta keys is accepted today (len(extra)==64) and now raises JsonBoundsError, so its whole metadata is discarded and {} is returned. That is inside the trigger and needs no fault. Criterion 10 names only refusal 'as rule-set key missing' (a rule-set case), so it does not name this departure. The disclosed Stricter entry concedes the departure: a dynamic row rule reading one of those keys now sees it missing, so the result differs from today's. The disclosure covers a different thing from extra coverage, because it changes the no-rule-set result the criterion requires to stay the same. It does not excuse the departure. So a request that runs today with the same result no longer does in this case.

  </details>

### 🟡 Suggestion / Minor (17)

<details><summary>17 items</summary>

1. `docs/external/rule-sets.md` line 99 says `sqllens serve` and `sqllens validate` both print a warning for an unconfirmed set. Only `validate` prints to the console; `serve` emits the warning through the `sqllens.rule_sets` logger before the server configures logging, so whether the operator sees it depends on the logging setup. (raised by 2/4 agents)
2. `docs/external/rule-sets.md` line 125 says every identifier is a decimal string so `"5"` and `5` are written the same way. That holds for a request value but not for the file, where a bare number fails validation, and the sentence sits in advice pointing the reader at the file's `binding.account_ids`. Line 145 of the same page also tells the operator to restart the server while the same sentence says the check is retried on the next request. (raised by 2/4 agents)
3. `docs/internal/database-connectors/read-only-safety.md` lines 185 and 191, `docs/internal/agent/factory.md` line 87 and `docs/internal/database-connectors/row-level-security.md` line 209 still give the runner call order without the two new runners, although a sibling line in the first file was scoped by this change. (raised by 2/4 agents)
4. The architecture tree in `AGENTS.md` gains no entry for `src/sqllens/rule_sets.py` or `src/sqllens/safety/rule_sets.py`, although it lists the safety package file by file and is the file coding agents read first. (raised by 2/4 agents)
5. `src/sqllens/cli.py` line 167 separates `_unconfirmed_rule_sets` from the function above it with one blank line where every other top-level definition uses two. The project's lint selection does not flag it. (raised by 1/4 agents)
6. `src/sqllens/cli.py` lines 99 to 119: `_rule_set_file_configured` answers false after swallowing a read or parse error, with no log record. On that path `verify-memory` tells the operator only that the configuration is bad, never that it does not support rule sets, which is the case the branch exists to cover. (raised by 1/4 agents)
7. `src/sqllens/server.py` lines 243 to 252 discard the whole of `_meta` at debug level when a future SDK stops exposing `model_fields_set`. With a rule-set file configured every request would then be refused as rule-set key missing, with nothing above debug to explain it, unlike the sibling extraction-failure branch, which warns. (raised by 1/4 agents)
8. `src/sqllens/rule_sets.py` lines 234 to 358 hold several invariants by call-site convention rather than in the types: the loaded-file docstring says the file is indexed for selection while both accessors scan or rebuild, `CatalogConfirmation.confirmed` is a public mutable latch that `src/sqllens/preflight.py` line 175 writes without taking the lock the type carries for it, `rule_sets` carries no minimum length so a file declaring no set loads cleanly, and `RuleSetSelection` constrains neither its set name nor its user number. (raised by 1/4 agents)
9. `src/sqllens/safety/rule_sets.py` lines 470 to 472 rebuild the refusal behind its own constructor, so a future stateful subclass would be re-raised half-built. (raised by 1/4 agents)
10. `src/sqllens/agent/factory.py` lines 91 to 105: the rule-set user resolver falls back to the shared built-in user with no log record when no selection is published, while every other rule-set component treats a missing selection as a refusal. (raised by 1/4 agents)
11. `src/sqllens/agent/core/system_prompt/default.py` lines 61 to 64, and `docs/internal/database-connectors/rule-sets.md` line 57, state that the rule-set flag adds both prompt rules without naming the two conditions that decide it: the qualify-every-column rule is added only when a dialect resolves, and neither rule is added when the caller supplies a base prompt. (raised by 1/4 agents)
12. The module docstring at `tests/connectors/test_rule_sets_mysql.py` line 8 describes the example set as listing a predicate column, but the module's shared example carries none; individual tests supply one. (raised by 1/4 agents)
13. `docs/internal/database-connectors/rule-sets.md` line 3 records a freshness marker five commits behind the branch head, all of them review-fix commits on the code the page describes. (raised by 1/4 agents)
14. `docs/external/configuration.md` line 234 still frames row-rule blocks as unlike other sections in rejecting unknown keys; the masking section already did, and the new rule-sets section does too. (raised by 1/4 agents)
15. Two criteria have no test anywhere: that `list_data_sources` answers a call carrying no request metadata while a rule-set file is configured, and that the bundle manifest gains no rule-set entry. (raised by 1/4 agents)

acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] With the new config key naming a valid version-1 rule-set file and a MySQL `database.url`, `sqllens validate` exits 0 and `sqllens serve` starts.
- [ ] A rule-set file with an unknown field in any record, a missing required field, a wrong-typed value (a Boolean where a number is expected, a TOML date for `generated_on` and a `role_id` other than its set's `name` included), an ID with a leading zero or a non-digit, an identifier outside `[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*`, a duplicate set or table name, a duplicate entry in any list (`columns = ["id", "name", "id"]` included), a predicate column also listed in `columns`, `metadata` key names that are not three distinct identifiers, or a `metadata` key name that SQL Lens reserves (`starter_ui_request`, `ui_features_available`) makes `sqllens validate` exit 2 and `sqllens serve` refuse to start, and the error names the record and the problem (at minimum these cases).
- [ ] A rule-set file whose `source` records hold only `confirmed_against_production` loads, and a file whose `source` records hold every provenance field the version-1 format defines loads unchanged.
- [ ] `sqllens validate` exits 2 and `sqllens serve` refuses to start, each with a message naming the cause, for a rule-set file that holds a `row_rule` (the message saying to remove the whole rule set, never only its row rules), for a non-MySQL `database.url`, and for a `binding.database` that differs from the database named in `database.url`, even when it equals `[database] name`.
- [ ] For a rule-set file with unconfirmed sets, `sqllens validate` exits 0 and prints one `Warning:` line naming each unconfirmed set, and `sqllens serve` starts and logs one warning naming each unconfirmed set.
- [ ] With a listed table or listed column missing from the connected MySQL database, a listed name whose letter case differs from the database's, or a listed table that is a view, `sqllens serve` (preflight on) refuses to start and `sqllens validate --check-db` exits 2, each naming the mismatched table or column.
- [ ] With `--no-preflight` and a listed column missing from the database, every rule-set request that passes the five request classes and the conversation-owner check is refused with `isError` before the agent runs, with text saying the rule-set file could not be confirmed against the database and naming no table or column. The server log names the missing column, and once the column exists the next such request is served. A request that also fails one of the five request classes is refused as that class.
- [ ] Each of exactly these five request classes is refused with `isError: true` before the agent runs, with text naming the class and no `_meta` value: rule-set key missing or empty; rule-set name not a string or whole number or naming no set; account key missing or its decimal text not in `binding.account_ids`; user key missing or not a positive whole number; the named set unconfirmed.
- [ ] A rule-set name sent as the number `2` or the string `"2"` selects set `"2"`, while `"02"`, `2.0`, `true`, `null`, `[2]` and `{}` are refused as naming no set.
